podcast_episode.title: Ebola surge, AI math shocker and daylight saving time
podcast_episode.name: Ebola surge, AI math shocker and daylight saving time
podcast_episode.description: In this week’s news roundup, we take a look at what’s happening with the Ebola outbreak in parts of Africa. Later SciAm editorial fellow Peter Hall joins host Rachel Feltman to discuss recent claims by OpenAI and Anthropic that their models have solved some of the world’s toughest math and physics problems. Plus, we dive into new research that suggests making daylight saving time permanent could put schoolchildren at risk. podcast_episode.title: Why we’re still obsessed with vampires
podcast_episode.name: Why we’re still obsessed with vampires
podcast_episode.description: In this Halloween special episode of Science Quickly, host Rachel Feltman explores why our fascination with vampires refuses to die. We dive into the spooky history of vampires—from tuberculosis outbreaks in the 18th and 19th centuries to sexy pop culture icons—and examine what our collective obsession with them says about us. Recommended Reading: Exhumed: Unearthing the History of the American Vampire. Aaron Mahnke. Running Press Adult, 2026 Recreational Fear Lab, co-directed by Mathias Clasen, at Aarhus University in Denmark “Monsters and Posttraumatic Stress: An Experiential-Processing Model of Monster Imagery in Psychological Therapy, Film and Television,” by Jenny Hamilton, in Humanities and Social Sciences Communications, Vol. 7, Article No. 142. podcast_episode.title: Reducing Treatment Burden While Preserving Sight [Sponsored]
podcast_episode.name: Reducing Treatment Burden While Preserving Sight [Sponsored]
podcast_episode.description: New approaches aim to extend treatment durability and improve long-term vision outcomes in wet AMD. Scientific American Custom Media recently sat down with Dr. Nadia Waheed, Ocular Therapeutix’s chief medical officer, to discuss the real-world burden behind the standard of care and how emerging approaches, including sustained-delivery therapies under investigation, aim to reduce it. podcast_episode.title: Why science is on the ballot in the midterms
podcast_episode.name: Why science is on the ballot in the midterms
podcast_episode.description: What does science have to do with the midterms? In this episode of Science Quickly, host Rachel Feltman speaks with Scientific American breaking news reporter Adam Kovac about candidates with science backgrounds, the future of Medicare for All, the role of evidence in policymaking and the election’s consequences for the broader scientific community.
